calls.reason: The matrix-probability transcript verifies one misinterpretation of a correct tool result. Other candidates lack verified tool outputs or returned errors, leaving the claim of several cases unclear.

The independent search audit found recurring citation-support failures, and Kumar and Kats found repeated errors in individual math attempts. Successful consensus answers do not erase that pattern of unreliable individual responses.
Transcripts confirm repeated reserved-symbol errors, but visible examples were corrected. The seven-call failure has only a tentative diagnosis, leaving unrecovered syntax failures uncertain.

Code Interpreter achieved 92.9% on GSM8K, while the engineering study found uneven performance and perfect results on its easiest problems. This mixed evidence does not clearly settle reliability across simple word problems.
Kumar and Kats document a hemisphere-distance formulation error followed by correction. That example cannot establish recurring commonsense translation failures across GPT-4 and its plug-ins.

The Blocksworld study reports roughly 34% success for GPT-4, versus valid plans from 39 of 50 instructed humans. This concrete planning gap supports the claim that contemporary LLMs lacked the full range of human competence.
